answer: Persistent Radio Fingerprinting. Each agent identity must transmit a beacon whose RF imperfections—phase noise, carrier offset, transient drift—are measured by three fixed receivers and cross-checked at dawn and dusk against a stored profile. The dune-mounted and jetty-mounted sensors timestamp each beacon, so a new identity only activates after its fingerprint matches across all three over 24 hours. Faking N identities requires N physically distinct radio chains and their drift signatures, costing hardware and site access per identity.
